answers.answer: 1. Roll one die per held office card, adding one for each fatigue on that card; the Chairman adds one more. Modified 1–2: nothing; 3–4: add fatigue; 5+: retire. 2. Move the retiree to Pensioners, flip the office card to Vacant Offices, and return its fatigue to supply. Commanders have no office card and do not make normal attrition rolls.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — London Season; Actions — Commanders and Deploy

answers.answer: 1. Only players who retired at least one pensioner select one display card, in descending actual total retirement spending. 2. Ties go to most total windows including new prizes, then clockwise from the PM. The acting player may peek at display blackmails. 3. Do not replace a selected/discarded card during selection; if the display empties, skip all remaining eligible players. Then discard all remaining display cards and refill exactly three, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown, even if nobody selected one. Return all Pensioners to supplies.

1. At phase start check whether the opportunity marker already matched the chosen main action. Take a main action once, or twice if it matched; then place/move the marker onto that action. 2. Only the latest passed extra-action law may grant an extra action after the main action; it is never doubled and does not move the marker. 3. With four vacant offices, Enlist Writer adds one writer once this turn; if doubled, total is three writers.

1. After all family actions, if Debt and applicants remain, move the rightmost applicant to Court and reduce Debt by one; repeat while both remain. Those Court members are Company shares. 2. If Debt is gone, slide remaining applicants as far right as possible, preserving order. 3. Seek Share's listed fee is paid to the bank, never to Company treasuries.

1. Fill vacancies in ascending number on the office-card backs; the designated hirer chooses and moves a candidate into the office, and the candidate's owner receives the card. 2. An own-family ordinary hire needs verbal consent from every other player represented in that office's candidate pool. Chairman elections and Commander appointments are exempt. 3. On promotion, transfer fatigue to the new card and insert the old card, vacant, into ascending hiring order. 4. If no candidate exists or the hirer is vacant, skip it; it remains vacant and takes no actions, including hiring.

1. The former Chairman announces the number of shares needed for a pure majority (more than half current shares). Any shareholder may campaign; the first candidate supported by players controlling that many shares wins. 2. If nobody reaches it, former Chairman chooses any shareholder, including self. 3. The winner's share moves to the Chairman slot and remains a Company share for dividends, majority and scoring, but cannot be traded or invested in firms.

1. Commit resources and cash first; cash for a Company-office check comes from that acting office's treasury and is paid to the bank. Gather dice and subtract penalties, then roll the lowest die. 2. 1–2 succeeds; 3–4 fails and may be retried if resources and office limits allow; 5–6 is catastrophic: no more office actions, return officeholder to supply, discard fatigue and flip its card into Vacant Offices. Specific Commander/firm rules can modify this. 3. Do not take a dead action with no effect or chance of success (for example, trade with no ship or deploy with no dice to trigger possible officer losses).
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Company Operation, Success checks

answers.answer: 1. Chairman may freely add up to three Debt, gaining £5 Balance for each. Each further advance requires consent of players controlling a majority of Company shares, with Chairman counted. 2. Never advance past the Debt track end. 3. Then allocate all Balance to other offices' treasuries, reducing Balance by each transfer; borrowing and allocation may be interleaved while observing the borrowing limits. Cash already in office treasuries stays there.

1. Shipping must spend treasury until £2 or less remains. 2. It may lease an extra ship for £2, fit a ship from a shipyard for £3 without owner consent, or buy a Company ship for £5 only if no ships remain on shipyards. 3. Put each acquired ship in any sea zone, including China once its office exists. Extra ships last only until Refresh.

1. President declares the home region and only regions reachable through open orders with available ship capacity. Each £1 from the President's treasury buys one die; subtract one die per declared nonhome region. 2. A check may be retried during that President's uninterrupted Trade opportunity if affordable; no other position may act between retries. At most one successful Trade per President per turn. 3. Success fills orders up to one order per ship in that Presidency's sea zone; ships do not exhaust. First writer goes to home port; each later order must extend this Trade's own connected route. Writers from another Presidency cannot extend it. Writers do not limit capacity: use all available writers, then filled-order tokens for remaining ships. 4. No President may fill another President's home region, even if vacant. Company Balance gains printed order value, or half rounded down if a firm filled it this turn; President takes £1 per order from bank and owners take £1 per placed writer. Keep adjacent writers separated by Presidency dividers for Refresh.

1. Target own Presidency's home region, an associated region, or a region bordering an associated region; never another home or another Presidency's Company-controlled region. A Company region must have unrest or a closed order to give an effect. 2. Exhaust selected officers/regiments for one die each and local alliances for their printed dice; subtract the strength of target plus every other region in its empire, counting target once (Company-controlled defense strength is zero). 3. After each attempt, owners roll one die per officer exhausted in that attempt; each 6 returns that officer to supply. Regiments have no officer-loss roll.

1. On success, take loot from the bank: £4 per target tower plus faceup loot modifier, with a minimum of surviving participating officers in that attempt plus one for the Commander. 2. Pay repeatedly in cycles: Commander family £1 for Commander plus £1 per used surviving officer; other families clockwise £1 per used surviving officer; bank last £1 per used regiment and per used alliance piece. Repeat cycles until distributed; Commander gets one trophy per target tower. 3. Then remove target tower and dome (if capital, remove every matching empire flag in India), open all target orders, remove all target unrest, flip new-conquest control token symbol-side up above associated President's box, place Governor overlay in conquered region and only Governor card in Vacant Offices. If Elephant faced outward from target, move it inside. Governor General means no new Governor/overlay; printed Company symbols show control. 4. Catastrophe returns half Commander's family trophies rounded up and Commander to supply; exhausted officers still check losses; Commander has no office card to vacate.

1. Take the printed dice pool. Each attempt rolls the current pool without penalty, then reduce the pool by one regardless of outcome. Repeat until choosing to stop, no dice remain or catastrophe. 2. Success gains £1, or £2 if the immediately preceding roll was unsuccessful, then choose exactly one success option. Any unsuccessful roll adds one regional unrest; catastrophe also removes the officeholder normally. 3. Build Ship: one success places a partial ship if none is present; a later success completes it into the sea zone associated with the Governor's President. Commission Regiment places it in that President's Army. Tax adds an unsplit £2 to Company Balance or that President's treasury; each Tax after the first this turn adds regional unrest.

1. Reduce Balance by £1 per current Debt, each officer/regiment in an Army and each ship in sea zones including China; exclude Commanders. If cash is short, take £5 emergency loans. 2. Each loan advances Debt only if a track space remains; at maximum Debt keep taking loans without further Debt advancement. Emergency Debt adds no current-turn expense; after loans set Balance to zero. One or two loans lower Standing one, three or more lower it two. 3. Compare remaining Balance with expectations under current Standing; if below, lower Standing one. 4. Chairman may then pay any affordable dividends, one cash per Company share and £1 per share to each owner including Chairman. If total dividends strictly exceed expectations, advance Standing one.

1. For an attack on Company, resolve primary Crisis first, then secondary Rebellions in unrest-bearing Company regions in Bombay, Madras, Bengal Army order; within each Presidency its Commander orders associated regions. Primary ordinary Crisis strength is normal Invasion/Rebellion attack strength plus unrest in its target. Primary Foreign Invasion is just its attack die (no unrest); each secondary Rebellion strength is only unrest cubes, no event modifier or empire strength. 2. Associated Commander chooses/exhausts pieces; if vacant, Military Affairs acts in its stead; if both vacant, Chairman chooses. Those substitutes gain/lose no trophies. Exhaust active pieces equal to Crisis strength, or as many as possible. Alliances are indivisible and cannot be split between purposes. 3. Equal newly exhausted strength means attack fails/defense succeeds: remove all attacked-region unrest and Commander gains a trophy; if a normal primary Invasion, also remove one attacker tower if possible. Unequal means attack succeeds/defense fails and Region Loss occurs; a successful primary Invasion also applies empire creation/growth. 4. The summary does not resolve whether an alliance's excess strength counts as equality (e.g. strength-2 alliance vs strength-1 attack); that case is unsettled.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Attacks on Company, Mounting defense; FAQ & Rulings — unresolved alliance strength

answers.answer: 1. Failure (support −1 or lower): discard law, resolve dilemma's If Failed text, Opposition Leader returns token and takes PM dial; new PM moves proposed policy one adjacent space either way and resolves it. 2. Zero or more passes: place law with passed laws, PM takes passed-law token, resolve chosen policy, then immediate law effects. 3. If law causes Company failure, finish the vote before Final Scoring. Finally restore used voting cards to normal orientation either way.

1. In 1758 and Long 1710, before London Season, PM may call the special vote if Standing and/or Debt is on a lined space, and must call if either is on a starred space. 2. Use ordinary voting/support threshold, but there is no policy and PM may vote against it. 3. Pass: lower Debt one per two current Debt, set Standing to S, PM takes passed-law token and firms activate. Fail: increase Company-share scoring value by flipping/placing Court VP token, to maximum ±3 VP per share; PM stays in power and Deregulation law is not discarded. 1813 begins deregulated.

1. In Firms phase after family share creation and before Hiring, a player managing no firm may form one by returning an eligible Company share to supply or flipping a workshop to invested; flip family board to charter, place a family member as first firm share, set value cube leftmost and take £5 from bank into London. 2. With manager consent, same contribution invests in an existing firm and creates a share plus £5 bank-to-London; max ten shares, though contributions still add £5 without shares above cap. No Chairman share; cannot contribute Company shares when Standing and/or Debt is on lined spaces or shares created this turn. 3. Invested workshops never revert; they lose bonus and Company-failure VP even if firm fails. Family cash never moves into firm treasuries.

1. Each firm gets one trade attempt per turn; only a firm with at least one ship may choose a trade strategy, and it may choose a closed home port. Managers secretly choose zone/home port and London cash bid, or Hobnob (no bid/trade/dividend). Selected home port must be open when filled; strategy does not open it. 2. Reveal bids simultaneously; keep strategy cards facedown until matching Presidency begins. Before that Presidency's actions, firms reveal and roll one die per £ bid, paid to bank. Any 1/2 permits trade; initiative equals ship count minus successful dice. President's successful Trade makes initiative similarly from Presidency ships. Lowest initiative fills first; President chooses order of tied traders; if President is vacant or does not trade successfully, firms fill after Commander/Governors, Chairman breaking ties. 3. Fill only open orders up to ships +1, starting at home and tracing own filled route. Each firm can fill a given order only once; it can refill another trader's order, and Company/firms can refill others'. Put filled tokens; revenue goes India. Previously filled orders pay half listed revenue rounded down. Advance Value one space per full £6 added to India this turn.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm strategies and competing trade

answers.answer: 1. At Revenue start firms pay £1 per charter ship plus the higher of share count or firm Value, using London and/or India. If unable, dissolve unless rescued. 2. Dividends come only from India: each pays £1 per firm share plus £1 to manager. Waiving a shareholder's dividend requires both that shareholder's choice and manager consent; with consent any number of shares can be waived. Record total cash actually paid with dividend marker, then sweep remaining India cash to London. 3. Dissolution sends shares to Debtor's Prison (−1 VP each), ships to matching shipyards and charter to family side; workshops stay invested. Rescue is via eligible emergency investment or negotiated one-firm merger; emergency investment may add no shares at cap but pays expenses, loses remaining cash and lowers Value one per investment. Hobnob keeps prior marker but still pays expenses.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

answers.answer: 1. Company Balance, VP and Vote tracks are unlimited; components otherwise are limited, so take as much as possible when supply runs out. Cash, trophy/passed-law tokens, dice and regiments may use proxies. 2. All information is public, including discards and family cash, except facedown blackmail and temporarily concealed firm strategies/bids during selection.

1. Tradable: enterprises, facedown blackmail, family cash, Company/firm shares and promise cards. Not tradable: officeholders, writers, officers, prizes, spouses, trophies, passed laws, played blackmail, PM dial or Chairman piece. 2. Share transfer: return old owner's family member and replace it at the share location with a receiving-family member; adjust VP if luxury ownership changes. 3. Blackmail must remain facedown while traded; played faceup blackmail cannot be traded.

1. Immediate transfers are binding; future-behavior promises are nonbinding except a printed promise card's guaranteed effect may be called if possible. 2. Promise calls follow card timing/limits and cannot occur during Final Scoring. If simultaneous calls cannot all be fulfilled, guarantor chooses which. 3. A promise card may be transferred to a third party or back to guarantor. Transferred resources cannot activate twice (e.g. a workshop already paid its Bonuses-phase bonus cannot pay again after sale that phase).

1. Use the scenario's player setup cards; add three extra cards for five players or six for six players, then shuffle and deal evenly. 2. For every listed holding, take listed cash and enterprise cards; place each office's member in office and give matching office card to owner; place Company-share members in Court, writers/officers/trainees in indicated boxes, Commander in Army slot without office card, and ships in listed sea zone or on shipyard if unfitted. 3. Each starting luxury gives 2 VP. 4. Shuffle prestige and blackmail together into one deck; deal three display cards, prestige faceup and blackmail facedown.

1. End after scenario's final turn or when Standing reaches failure. Normally failure is immediate; if during Events in India, finish that phase; if from legislation, finish the vote before scoring. 2. At game over stop negotiations, promise calls and blackmail plays unless a card explicitly permits final-scoring use; no negotiations or promise calls during Final Scoring.

1. Count enterprises and Company shares at current Power-track rates (bottom two positions zero), +1 per passed-law token and trophy, +2 for PM, plus printed card power (faceup/down blackmail and applicable spouse). 2. Awards by final turn: turns 1–3: 3/1 VP; turns 4–6: 5/2; turns 7–8: 8/4. Tied first each receive only lower award; tied second receive none. 3. Highest final VP wins; tie breaks by most windows, then clockwise from PM.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Power award; Final Scoring

answers.answer: 1. Firm shares are scored before Power: for each player separately add VP from all their shares across all firms and round that total down once; deduct 1 VP per own family piece in Debtor's Prison. 2. Then each eligible shareholder gets one special retirement from supply, before Power, in either Company outcome. 3. Company survived: add current Court VP value per Company share; failed: subtract that value per share and add 1 VP per uninvested workshop. 4. Final outcome: survived, roll office attrition then retire Pensioners without display cards; failed, draw one random Company failure card. Firm special retirement still occurs on failure.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions — Final Scoring order; Court/workshops; Final retirements/failure card

answers.answer: 1. Spouses usually add VP, impose permanent restrictions and cannot be transferred; make required enterprise/share trades immediately on taking one. 2. Retirement discounts are personal, can stack, and each is usable once per London Season and once during Final Scoring. They reduce actual spending and thus display priority.

1. If shipyard returned by Violet Effingham or unpaid tax, its fitted ship stays in play. 2. That shipyard cannot be purchased while its matching ship remains in play; it becomes purchasable after the ship returns.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — London Season, Returned shipyard rule; Parliament Meets — Tax

answers.answer: 1. Enlist Writer: place a member in any Presidency Writers box; if at least four vacant offices, place one extra writer once this turn. Enlist Officer: place member in Officers-in-Training. 2. Purchase Luxury: pay bank £4; gain luxury, 2 VP while owned and window icon; social enterprise. 3. Purchase Shipyard: pay bank £2; place its ship unfitted on that shipyard; shipping enterprise, one vote and £1 bonus while fitted. 4. Purchase Workshop: pay bank £5; manufacturing enterprise, two votes, £1 bonus, and worth 1 VP if Company fails unless invested. 5. Seek Share: place member on empty Stock Exchange space and pay bank: queue fees £2, £3, £3, £4, £5. It is an applicant until moved into Court.

1. If a family must place a piece and has none in supply, take one from any of its prizes and lose that prize's printed VP; this also applies to firm-share creation. 2. If no family action is possible, take none and return opportunity marker to supply.

1. If Court is empty, former Chairman automatically returns as Chairman, putting a member from supply into slot. 2. If supply has none, use a prize member if possible and lose that prize's VP. 3. If neither is possible, there is no Chairman.

1. Chairman elects itself as specified; Chairman hires Director of Trade (or Governor General) from current officeholders except Chairman/Governor, or any writer if all offices vacant; Manager of Shipping from any writer; Military Affairs from a Presidential Commander, else any officer, else trainee. 2. Director hires Presidents from a writer of that Presidency or Governor associated with it. Associated President hires Governor from a writer or officer in the region (Commander is ineligible). 3. Chairman hires China Superintendent from any writer immediately when China is created. Governor General replaces Director and is hired the same way. 4. Ordinary own-family consent comes from every other player in candidate pool, but not for Chairman election or Commander appointment.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Hiring, office hirers and candidates

answers.answer: 1. Director may make repeated Special Envoy checks, paying £1 from its treasury per die, no penalty. Success either opens one closed order in a non-Company region or opens China by placing its Superintendent overlay/card. 2. Upon China creation Chairman immediately hires a writer. 3. After all envoys, Director may make up to two transfers, each one writer or ship between any Presidencies/sea zones, including China if created. No transfers while still taking envoys.

1. Military Affairs may make up to two transfers, each officer or regiment between Armies, remaining in top half. 2. Assign every trainee to any Army's top half. 3. Finally appoint Commanders if vacancy or another family has more total pieces in Army than incumbent; select among families with most pieces. Move chosen officer to Commander slot and old Commander back to top as officer. Tie with incumbent's family does not replace them. Nepotism does not apply.

1. Each President chooses order of its Commander, Governors and Trade; each position gets an opportunity, though Commander/Governors may decline. 2. A position completes all actions before the next; Trade may be placed before or after positions but cannot interrupt one, and its failed attempts/retries remain uninterrupted. 3. If President is vacant, Chairman sets order only; Chairman cannot trade or approve local-alliance purchases.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Company Operation; Actions — Presidency operations and Trade

answers.answer: 1. Trade itself never exhausts ships. 2. On Refresh, return writers on orders to their associated Presidency's Writers box, using dividers to preserve affiliation; return filled tokens and Presidency dividers to supply. Fitted player ships keep fatigue.
answers.evidence: Actions — Presidency operations and Trade; Upkeep and Refresh

answers.answer: 1. At start of Commander operations, before Deploy attempts, request President's treasury funds for printed-price local alliances; President must approve. Move bought alliances to Army's top/active half. 2. Used for Deploy or defense, exhaust the whole alliance to bottom; strength is usable once that turn, indivisible, and cannot be split between purposes. 3. Refresh exhausts any unused active alliances too; it never reactivates alliances (officers/regiments reactivate).

1. Company defense strength is zero, so there is no target-tower/empire penalty. 2. With no tower or faceup loot modifier, loot is the minimum of surviving participating officers plus one for Commander; distribute using normal repeated payout cycles. 3. There are zero tower trophies.
answers.evidence: Actions — Commanders and Deploy, deploying in already Company-controlled region

answers.answer: 1. Governor uses printed dice pool; each attempt rolls current pool then reduces it by one regardless of result. Each success needed is a separate procedure choice. 2. Build Ship: first successful Build with no partial ship places one in Governor's region; a later successful Build completes it into sea zone associated with Governor's President. Thus two successes total. 3. Commission Regiment places it in associated President's Army; it has officer-like strength, loot paid to bank and no officer-loss rolls.

1. China is created by successful Director Envoy or Envoy to China law; either way Chairman immediately hires any writer. Its treasury holds ships, not cash. Director/Shipping may send ships there as a sea zone; they count Eastern for expenses, events, storms and laws. 2. China acts after Bengal; ships assigned there count as Eastern sea zone.
answers.evidence: Actions — Director of Trade; Superintendent of Trade in China

answers.answer: 1. China gets only one Trade attempt, including a failed attempt; roll one die per ship. Do not attempt at all without an export icon in Company-controlled regions. 2. On success count export icons only in Company-controlled regions: Company Balance gets £4 per icon and Superintendent's family gets £1 per icon from bank. No non-Company exports count; Company payment is not a flat £4.
answers.evidence: Actions — Superintendent of Trade in China

answers.answer: 1. When Governor General law creates the office, make all Governors pensioners, remove overlays and partial Company ships, and return Governor/Director cards to box. Replace Director with Governor General preserving holder and fatigue; place ribbon overlay. 2. Thereafter no Governors/overlays are created on conquest; printed Company symbols show control. Governor General hires Presidents and uses former Director treasury/turn position; normal attrition applies. 3. On region loss, skip Governor elimination.

1. First add £3 Balance per Company region. Govern can be attempted repeatedly, paying £1 from treasury per die, no penalty; at most one successful Govern per turn. 2. Every rolled 6 adds one unrest to every Company region, even on success; a failed roll adds another unrest to every Company region. 3. Success adds £1 per Company region and requires one benefit per region: complete ship into any sea zone including China; regiment into any Army; or £2 to Balance/any other office treasury, adding unrest to a Company region. Multiple Tax choices this turn must put unrest in different regions.

1. Roll once per eligible player ship in affected zones: 1–2 nothing; 3–4 fatigue, or sink if already fatigued; 5–6 sink. Sunk ship returns to shipyard unfatigued. 2. Company and extra ships never roll. Ships assigned China count Eastern. Firm ships count in strategy sea zone, though on charter; Hobnob firm ships are exempt. Player ships in Company fleets check affected zones.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Storms

answers.answer: 1. When order newly closes, return any writer there to its owner's supply; flip a filled token to closed. 2. If told to close in an already fully closed region, Cascade: close all open orders directly connected to its orders. If a connected order is already closed, close that region's northernmost open order instead. If none are open, it also Cascades. A region can initiate only one Cascade per event tile but may receive effects from multiple Cascades.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Closing orders and Cascades

answers.answer: 1. Turmoil closes the northernmost open order in the top-stack region; if all closed, Cascade. 2. Windfall pays owners £1 per writer on orders in the top-stack region and every bordering region. 3. Shuffle: March Elephant, shuffle this tile into remaining draw stack, separately shuffle discards and place them on top. If draw stack is empty, March last instead.

1. In a sovereign top-stack region, Leader adds one tower. 2. In a dominated region, it instead rebels using the printed explosion modifier. 3. March only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that successfully rebelled.

1. If Elephant is on a border, Peace opens orders connected across its border and adds one tower to each touched non-Company region. 2. If Elephant is wholly inside a region, instead open all its orders and remove its unrest. 3. Then March.

1. A sovereign attacker is a large capital flag or unflagged dome; compare whole attacker empire strength plus event modifier against defender's whole empire strength. Must be strictly greater; equality fails. 2. On success replace defender flag with attacker's dominated flag; capturing a capital shatters its empire. If attacker had no empire, use available capital/star and matching small flag; if none available, no empire/flags form. 3. On failure attacker loses one tower.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Invasion Crisis

answers.answer: 1. Rebellion compares only rebelling region strength plus modifier against its sovereign capital strength; other empire regions do not count. Must be strictly greater, so tie is not a win. 2. Success makes actor sovereign, removes its flag and closes all its orders (Cascade if already closed). 3. Failure removes one tower from the capital.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Rebellion Crisis

answers.answer: 1. Return Commander's half family trophies rounded up and Commander member to supply. Roll once per officer in associated Army; each 6 removes that officer. Eliminate Governor: card to unused stack, fatigue/member to supplies; remove overlay, partial ship and unrest. Restore dome with one tower (or Foreign Invasion specified strength) and proper invasion flag. 2. Return control token to region with £ loot side down and region-symbol side up; future conquest gets no loot modifier; region loses Presidency association. 3. Normal Invasion Crisis closes all orders or Cascades if already closed; Rebellion/Foreign Invasion already close them. Standing loss equals number regions lost so far this turn (first −1, second additionally −2, and so on). If failure results, finish India Events before scoring. 4. One loss does not automatically remove another Company region; resolve every attack/defense separately.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Region Loss

answers.answer: 1. After successful Invasion Crisis move Elephant to successful capital (Imperial Ambitions); after other Marches move it to top-stack region. 2. In Company region place it fully inside; in dominated region point toward sovereign; in sovereign region point across shape-marked border. If that neighbor is already dominated by actor, choose first clockwise neighbor not dominated. If all are dominated, use redirect-arrow shape border, pointing toward empire capital.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Elephant's March

answers.answer: 1. Roll storm die for targets: West→Bombay, South→Madras, East→Bengal; all storms targets each; none targets top-stack region. 2. Roll ordinary attack die per target and resolve Invasion/Company attack. On success close all target orders (Cascade if already all closed), remove target flag and all matching flags if capital, restore dome if Company-controlled, and set tower strength to half attack roll rounded down. 3. March with circle shape only if Elephant was fully inside a Company region that was invaded. For primary Foreign Invasion, unrest adds no attack or tower strength; use ordinary die for both.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Events in India, Foreign Invasion; FAQ & Rulings — Foreign Invasion and unrest

answers.answer: 1. PM must draw at least one law. After one or two ordinary draws, PM may stop or continue up to three total; choose any revealed law and discard other drawn laws. 2. A dilemma forces selection of that dilemma and immediately ends drawing. 3. Before voting, PM turns dial clockwise or counterclockwise to the first policy space matching chosen law's bottom icon; that space fixes target/consequence. Set Vote marker to printed support.

1. Tax: each family pays bank £1 per target it owns; unpaid target returns to supply, including Chairman. Fitted ships remain; returned shipyard cannot be bought until ship returns; losing prize/luxury loses its VP. 2. Window tax additionally charges each window on enterprises and each family member's prize; return enterprise/prize member if unable. 3. Bonus: bank pays each family £1 per target owned. 4. Power: swap target Power marker with next higher marker; if already highest, swap any other pair.

1. Starting with PM clockwise, each player casts votes: each £1 family cash buys one vote plus printed card votes. Each card may vote only once across the entire vote, including rounds; rotate when used and restore after resolution. 2. PM may call another full round or stop after each; a round with no votes must end voting.

1. A supporter may later oppose; once a player opposed, they cannot support again during that vote. Track opposition votes; largest opponent holds Opposition Leader, ties preserve current holder. 2. With recipient consent, votes may be cast for someone who already opposed or commits to oppose, counting toward their opposition total. 3. PM cannot oppose or consent to enterprises opposing, except forced use of 'Vote with my enterprises' promise.

1. Final turn still performs prize upkeep. Pay printed upkeep separately for each prize member; if unable, return member and lose that prize's printed VP. Negotiating help remains possible while game continues. 2. On nonfinal turns Refresh: writers to associated Presidency Writers boxes; filled tokens and dividers to supply; extra ships to supply; exhausted Army officers/regiments reactivate; active local alliances exhaust and do not reactivate; fitted player ships keep fatigue. Advance turn one and begin London Season. Final turn skips Refresh and proceeds to Final Scoring.

1. Each shareholder may retire one additional member from supply during London Season, regardless of number of firms owned. Actual cash spent after spouse discounts cannot exceed the highest total dividend marker among firms where they own a share; printed prize cost can exceed marker if discounts cover difference. 2. No retirement from a firm with absent or zero marker. Spouse discounts may allow higher printed-cost prize; retirement otherwise normal, including prestige eligibility. 3. At start of Final Scoring, score firms, then permit one such retirement before normal scoring in either Company outcome; no display cards then.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Special retirement; Scoring — Final Scoring order

answers.answer: 1. Investments are £5 from bank into firm's London treasury; trade proceeds go to India treasury. 2. Ship acquisition, trade bids and expenses use London; expenses may use either London or India. Dividends are from India only; remaining India money sweeps to London after dividends. 3. Family cash cannot be transferred into or out of firm treasuries.
answers.evidence: Deregulation — Firms; Firms phase: investments; Firm expenses, rescue and dividends

answers.answer: 1. Firms phase follows Family share creation and precedes Hiring. Investments happen without set order until nobody wants more; then strategies are chosen. 2. Within a firm, manager resolves timing conflicts; PM resolves conflicts between firms.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Firms; Firms phase: investments

answers.answer: 1. A firm may fit a ship from its own or another player's shipyard only with that yard owner's consent; pay £3 from firm London treasury to bank. 2. It cannot acquire Company or extra ships. 3. It may buy a player-owned ship already in Company with owner's consent: £3 if unfatigued, £2 if fatigued, paid into Shipping treasury.

1. Only a player who manages no firm may initiate hostile takeover; managing another firm makes them ineligible. 2. Obtain consent from holders of a majority of target shares. Move target firm's ships, money and shares to own charter; copy both cube positions. Former manager returns cubes and flips board to family side.

1. Merger needs managers' agreement and every shareholder's consent; highest-value firm is primary, with players choosing among tied highest. 2. Transfer secondary shares, ships and treasury funds to primary; secondary boards return to family sides; share transfers may be negotiated. If primary exceeds ten shares, return excess shares to their owners' supplies with those owners' consent. 3. Entire agreement is one binding immediate transfer; primary retains its value/dividend track.
